3-(2-Furoyl)-quinoline-2-carboxaldehyde
(
FQ
) is a
fluorogenic
amine labeling dye that is not fluorescent itself,  but reacts with
primary amines
to form fluorescent products.
[
1
]
It was first reported in 1990.
[
2
]
Cyanide
, typically provided via
KCN
or
NaCN
salts, is a required co-substrate in the fluorogenic reaction.
[
3
]
It has been used for the detection of
amines
and
peptides
, largely in CE-SDS, where it is recognized to reach a
silver stain
-like high sensitivity via
laser-induced fluorescence
.
[
4
]
Once bound to protein the excitation wavelength is 480 nm (blue) and the emission wavelength is ~600 nm (orange).
[
5
]
